attack: Carry-is-king's 140bp coupon is the mispricing, not the trade: a 3.8th-percentile CA-US 2Y already embeds BoC-easier-than-Fed. The hawk owns compression of that spread via delayed CA easing or a hike bias, not collection of a spread that inflation persistence should not justify.

Dollar-king's 'USDCAD has not caught the rate gap' reading is one-sided. Alternative: the rate gap is the unjustified object. Spot at the 74th 1y percentile with a still-negative 3m return has not confirmed a completed CAD-weakness regime matching a 0.20th-percentile CA-US 10Y.

Catalyst-junkie dates CAD cheapening to this week's G10 tightening plus a reduced oil-supply tail. That sequence is USD-known and CAD-incomplete: BoC minutes named pass-through as a risk, headline is stuck at 3%, and the desk thesis says energy is constraining the global easing impulse, including Canada's.

Trend-follower's 1d/5d/1m alignment is flow after a >90% priced hike, not new CA policy information. CA activity 53.2 versus US 49.92 and Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q versus US deceleration to +1.5% SAAR do not support treating CAD as the soft cyclical that must keep cheapening.

Saudi workaround is not a CAD-policy green light. Fact is tail reduction with modest oil easing; inference that energy/CAD ToT and pass-through are dead overstates a single-source workaround against retained crude-near-$110 and weakened shock absorbers.
defense: Labor cooling is the real hole in the hawk case and remains the invalidation, not the base case: CA labor score 48.8, employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y versus +2.8%. Headline held at 3.0% with BoC-named energy pass-through and the strongest activity gauge in the emphasis set still argue CA policy risk is underpriced to the upside.
Paying the 140bp 2Y proxy is the cost of owning that inflation discrepancy. Carry is adverse, not disqualifying, while the closing mechanism is CA yields up / USDCAD down rather than a Fed pivot.

US inflation is not the residual hawk trade: August CPI already kept the Fed tightening bias intact and the hike was pre-priced. Residual upside policy risk is in CAD, where core-near-target pricing ignores stuck headline and energy pass-through.
AUDCAD/AUDUSD expressions own Australian housing or valuation, not the CA inflation/reaction-function gap. Hawk expression stays USDCAD.
Concede if incoming Canadian CPI shows energy failing to lift headline or core while labor deterioration continues, revealing the CA-US discount as warranted easier policy.
holes_in_opposing_case: FACT: CA-US 2Y is -140bp on 2026-09-17 at the 3.8th 1y and 4.3rd 5y percentile, still widening 15bp over 5d and 17bp over 1m. INFERENCE: that extremity is the market-implied assumption that BoC can stay far easier than the Fed. Collecting it as carry is owning the priced conclusion, not an edge; the hawk discrepancy is that CA inflation/pass-through should compress the gap. Carry-is-king even states that fading USDCAD requires the 140bp to close faster than carry accrues, which is the hawk closing mechanism, not a reason to stay long USD.

FACT: the 16 Sep Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% entered with greater-than-90% odds and is now delivered. INFERENCE: dollar-king/catalyst-junkie treat a completed, pre-priced US event plus BoJ/BoE as live USD-hawk alpha versus CAD. Known information needs new transmission; the residual underpriced hawk risk sits in the currency still priced for easier policy, not in the one that just hiked.

FACT: Canada headline CPI held at 3.0% y/y; CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%; BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through; retained energy research still has crude near $110 with tight refined-fuel buffers; last24 desk says the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse. INFERENCE: using core-near-2% to declare no BoC catch-up is composition-blind in an energy-shock regime. The Saudi/Oman workaround only reduced the extreme oil-supply tail and prices eased modestly; it did not remove the still-elevated crude level that feeds pass-through. UNKNOWN: the packet has no BoC OIS path, so 'no live hike catalyst' is inferred from core, not from a priced BoC distribution.

FACT: CA 2Y is 3.27% at the 97.8th 1y percentile and CA 10Y is 3.83% at the 97.4th; US 2Y is 4.67% at the 99.2nd. INFERENCE: opponents tag CA_RATES_DOWN as if Canada were in an easing gap, but locally Canadian yields are already historically high. The cheapness is relative to an even more extreme US front end. A BoC reaction-function shift on energy pass-through can compress CA-US from the CA side without Fed easing.

FACT: packet has no forward points, OIS, or executable FX carry; USDCAD 3m return is still -1.25% while 1y percentile is only 74th versus a 4th-percentile rate gap. INFERENCE: the 140bp holding cost is a 2Y sovereign proxy, not verified FX carry. Trend-follower's 5d/1m grind (+1.10%/+1.74%) is post-known-hike price action, not proof the inflation discrepancy is closed.

catalysts: Next Canadian CPI print that lifts headline or core via energy/food pass-through
Subsequent BoC communications that convert the minutes' pass-through warning into a delayed-easing or hike-bias reaction function
Persistence of crude near the retained $110 shock-absorber regime
US data that stops adding US-only front-end premium
evidence_refs: rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
revised_trade.invalidation: BoC communication or incoming Canadian CPI shows energy failing to lift headline/core while labor deterioration continues, so the CA-US discount is revealed as warranted easier policy rather than underpriced inflation risk.
revised_trade.mispricing: CA-US 2Y at -140bp (3.8th one-year percentile) and CA-US 10Y at -111bp (0.20th one-year percentile) assume BoC can stay far easier than the Fed because core is near 2%; that ignores stuck 3% headline CPI, BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through, Canadian activity/consumer still above 52, and crude near $110.
principal_risks: Core staying near 2% and wages/employment continuing to cool
Saudi/Oman workaround collapsing the oil tail
Paying 140bp of US-CA 2Y carry while the reprice is delayed
Further Fed tightening that widens CA-US again
revised_trade.thesis: Canadian headline inflation persistence plus BoC energy pass-through risk are underpriced relative to a historically extreme CA-US yield discount after a fully anticipated Fed hike, so CAD policy restraint should reprice higher and USDCAD lower.
why_now: Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% was greater-than-90% priced and is now known; residual hawk risk has migrated to currencies still priced for easier policy.
BoC minutes already flag higher energy pass-through while August CPI held at 3% and CA-US spreads cheapened further over the month.
Energy shock absorbers remain weak and the last24 desk says the shock is constraining the global easing impulse.

strongest_opponent_point: The verified CA-US 2Y of about 140bp is paid to long USDCAD while Canadian core near 2% and cooling labor give opponents a coherent case that BoC will not catch the Fed fast enough to beat carry.
